get.summary: Lists company schedules through one filtered, ordered, and paged read.
get.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. For a company-scoped manager the result is restricted, never refused: every query path returns only rows whose schedule assignee set intersects the manager's reach or is empty, and pagination figures describe the restricted set. Read-tier counted history includes ended memberships; where a shift-group set also contributes participations, cancelled, conflict-excluded, and removed rows still count. Every accepted request uses the same result path and server-derived lifecycle state. Omitting `state` applies no lifecycle-state filter; omitting `page` and `limit` applies and reports page 1 with a page size of 50. Absent `sort`, results are ordered by name then identifier; a `sort` value orders the requested fields left to right, always followed by an implicit ascending identifier tie-break. The retired `skip` parameter is rejected; use `page` and `limit` for paging. Omitting `state` applies no lifecycle-state filter. When present, `state` accepts equivalent repeated-key (`state=Draft&state=Active`) and comma-separated (`state=Draft,Active`) forms. Tokens are trimmed and matched case-insensitively; pipe-separated values and empty items inside a value that names at least one state are also accepted. A present value that names no state, mixes comma and pipe separators, or contains any unsupported token yields `400` addressed to `state`, and no part of the filter is applied. `sort` is an optional query value of the form `{field} {asc|desc}[,{field} {asc|desc}]` naming one to seven of the allowlisted fields `name`, `startUtc`, `endUtc`, `repeatUntilDate`, `assignedEmployeeCount`, `color`, and `displayState`, each followed by a mandatory `asc` or `desc` direction; matching is case-insensitive and the separating space may be encoded as `%20` or `+`. The default order absent `sort` is `name asc`; every ordering — explicit or default — is followed by an implicit ascending identifier tie-break, so the result is always a total order. `repeatUntilDate` places schedules with no value last in both directions. Ordering by `displayState` uses the same published lifecycle rank (`Draft`=0, `Active`=1, `Future`=2, `Past`=3) returned in Worklio.ApiModels.SCH.Models.Schedules.ScheduleListItem_v10.Status; the sort key remains `displayState`. Ordering by `assignedEmployeeCount` uses the same value and the same moment as the returned Worklio.ApiModels.SCH.Models.Schedules.ScheduleListItem_v10.AssignedEmployeeCount. Examples: `?sort=name asc`, `?sort=startUtc desc`, `?sort=displayState asc,name asc`, `?sort=assignedEmployeeCount desc,name asc`. A blank or whitespace-only `sort` value, an unrecognized field or direction, a missing direction, an empty or duplicated term, more than seven terms, or a repeated `sort` query key all yield `400` addressed to field `sort`, with no part of the value applied and no silent fall-back to the default order.

Optional server-derived lifecycle-state filter supplied as repeated keys or a
comma-separated value; both forms are equivalent. Omitting it applies no lifecycle filter.

parameters.description: Optional one-based page number; defaults to 1 and is always reported.

parameters.description: Optional page size from 1 through 200; defaults to 50 and is always reported.

parameters.name: sort

post.summary: Creates a schedule in the draft lifecycle state.
post.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. For a company-scoped manager only the reach precondition applies: the operation addresses no persisted resource and names no employee, so it is refused only when the manager's reach cannot be established. Validates recurrence, time-zone, and job-cost references before persisting the draft and returns its canonical representation and concurrency token.

get.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. A company-scoped manager reads at the read tier: at least one assignee of the schedule must be within the manager's reach, or the schedule must have no assignees; otherwise the response is the not-found shape. Read-tier counted history includes ended memberships; where a shift-group set also contributes participations, cancelled, conflict-excluded, and removed rows still count. The schedule must exist in the requested company. Drafts, published schedules, and past schedules are all returned, including the concurrency token that ending or duplicating the schedule requires.

patch.summary: Applies a JSON Merge Patch to a draft or published schedule.
patch.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. A company-scoped manager changes at the change tier: every assignee of the schedule must be within the manager's reach; an intersecting but not contained assignee set is refused access-denied and a disjoint one answers not-found. For a draft update, manager change threshold measured over: memberships effective on or after the earlier of the stored and proposed schedule start days. For a published-series retime, manager change threshold measured over: memberships effective on or after the scope-dependent retime day, united with counted participants of every live occurrence the requested retime touches. For a published non-reshaping update, the same threshold as an EntireSeries change is used: memberships effective today, united with counted participants of every live future occurrence. Outside the FutureOccurrences time-anchor rules below, omitted schedule-content properties keep their current values; explicit null clears nullable content properties where the field contract permits it. Changing recurrence type requires the complete recurrence configuration group. Draft behavior is unchanged. A published repeating schedule requires `applyTo` only when the patch sets at least one reshaping field: `timeZoneId`, `startUtc`, `endUtc`, `recurrenceType`, `recurrenceInterval`, `daysOfWeek`, `monthWeekOrdinal`, `recurrenceDurationDays`, `repeatUntilDate`, `rotationDaysOn`, `rotationDaysOff`, `rotationLengthWeeks`, or `rotationWeeks`. A stated scope on a repeating schedule is always honoured. A published patch that states no scope and sets none of those fields updates only the schedule master and audit history; it does not reshape shifts or repetition rows. A stated scope or any reshaping field is refused for a published one-time schedule. `effectiveFromUtc` is refused when no scope is stated. EntireSeries redraws the original schedule's unstarted future only when the patch sets a reshaping field. FutureOccurrences does not rewrite the addressed schedule into the new future series. It bounds that original before `effectiveFromUtc` and creates a fresh linked continuation anchored on that UTC calendar date. Time and recurrence values present in the request body configure the continuation. If `startUtc` is present, its UTC date must equal `effectiveFromUtc`; a mismatch returns HTTP 400 on `startUtc`. If `startUtc` is omitted, the server rebases the existing proposed start—the current canonical start in that case—onto the cutoff while preserving its UTC time of day. If `endUtc` is omitted, the continuation preserves the current source shift duration. Every successful patch returns one result shape. `resultType` is `DraftUpdated`, `PublishedScheduleUpdated`, `EntireSeriesUpdated`, or `FutureOccurrencesSplit`, according to the operation performed. `schedule` is always the refreshed route-addressed schedule, and `continuation` is always emitted but is non-null only for a future-occurrences split. Every later operation intended for that future series must address the returned `continuation.id`, using its returned row version where concurrency is required; continuing to use the original identifier addresses only the bounded original series.

parameters.name: scheduleId
parameters.description:
Identifier of the Draft or Active schedule being patched. After FutureOccurrences succeeds,
later operations on the new future series use the returned `continuation.id` instead.

requestBody.description:
Merge-patch document including the current row version. For FutureOccurrences its supplied
time and recurrence values describe the new continuation, and `effectiveFromUtc` is that
continuation's UTC cutoff and anchor.

200.description:
Returns one unified schedule-patch result for `DraftUpdated`,
`PublishedScheduleUpdated`, `EntireSeriesUpdated`, and
`FutureOccurrencesSplit` outcomes. The continuation is present as null for every
non-split outcome.

post.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. A company-scoped manager changes at the change tier: every assignee of the schedule must be within the manager's reach; an intersecting but not contained assignee set is refused access-denied and a disjoint one answers not-found. Manager change threshold measured over: memberships effective on or after the later of the schedule start and 24 hours before the publish instant. The operation captures one UTC instant, re-validates the complete stored draft, and atomically activates, audits, and materializes it. A failed publish preserves the draft and creates no occurrence or Published audit row. Before materialization, every window-effective member is re-checked for participation overlaps. A conflict returns 409 `SCH_ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT` naming the affected employees and schedules; the draft and its memberships remain unchanged. A successful publish stamps each member onto the materialized, not-yet-ended occurrences covered by that membership window. Activation, audit, occurrence materialization, and the participant snapshot commit atomically, so any failure rolls back the complete publish.

Manager change threshold measured over: memberships effective through the requested schedule end day, united with participants of live, uncancelled occurrences starting after that day. The end date is today or later and is the last worked day: a shift on that date is kept and every shift starting after it is cancelled. Day boundaries are judged on the UTC calendar and a shift belongs to the UTC date it starts on, so an overnight shift starting on the end date is kept. Manager change threshold measured over: schedule memberships effective through the requested range start when a schedule is named; otherwise the resource set is empty. Current scheduled minutes use active participation plus deterministic future estimates; proposed minutes are gross and time-off minutes are null when the optional time-off source is unavailable. Membership-window and undecided shift blockers are returned together as a normal HTTP 200 result with `canAssign` false. The operation opens no write transaction, takes no application lock, persists and reserves nothing, and guarantees nothing about a later create. The reported `evaluatedAtUtc` is the evaluation's reference clock, not a snapshot, lease, token, or concurrency value. patch.summary: Changes one shift's time or its job-costing.
patch.description: Access: System, Admin, ClientAdmin, and company-scoped Manager users. A company-scoped manager changes at the change tier: every assignee of the shift group must be within the manager's reach; an intersecting but not contained assignee set is refused access-denied and a disjoint one answers not-found. Manager change threshold measured over: owning-schedule memberships effective on or after the earliest shift-group start day, united with every counted participation in the addressed group, including cancelled, conflict-excluded, and removed rows. The request carries exactly one change kind — a time change or a job-costing change — and the employee it is addressed to decides its reach. Without an employee it covers the whole shift, including every per-employee variant, and is refused whole if any part of the shift has started or is cancelled. With an employee it covers that employee alone: the shift is changed directly when they are its only active assignee, and otherwise they receive their own variant at the new value while everyone else keeps the original untouched. A time change is checked against every affected employee's other shifts, so it can never double-book anyone, and it must land strictly in the future. A shift whose time was changed by hand is marked, which protects it from being overwritten by background generation; changing it back to the generated time clears the mark again. Omitted properties are left unchanged. The preferred time zone travels with its local start and end as one unit and is stored exactly as supplied, without conversion. An optional note is recorded with the change in schedule history and is shown to employees on notifications the time change already produces. The server captures one UTC operation instant. Without an employee, the group change is refused atomically when any occurrence part it would write has `startUtc <= serverOperationTimeUtc`. With an employee, only the physical occurrence addressed by `occurrenceId` is evaluated. The cutoff is inclusive and uses the current start, not the end. HTTP 409 then carries code `SCH_OCCURRENCE_IMMUTABLE`. Clients may use calendar `startUtc` values to disable editing pre-emptively, but must still handle the conflict because of elapsed time and client/server clock differences.

requestBody.description: The change and the matching concurrency tokens.

Manager change threshold measured over: owning-schedule memberships effective on or after the earliest shift-group start day, united with every counted participation in the addressed group, including cancelled, conflict-excluded, and removed rows. The cancellation covers every part of the shift, so no per-employee variant is left active. A shift that is only partly cancelled is completed: the still active parts are cancelled and the already cancelled ones keep their own record. Only a shift with nothing left active is refused. The optional reason is written into the schedule history at this moment, so it stays available even after the shift is restored. The server captures one UTC operation instant and evaluates only the currently active occurrence parts that this request would cancel. The cancellation is refused atomically when any such part has `startUtc <= serverOperationTimeUtc`. The cutoff is inclusive and uses the start, not the end. HTTP 409 then carries code `SCH_OCCURRENCE_IMMUTABLE`. Already cancelled parts remain unchanged and do not block the request on this rule. Clients may disable cancellation from calendar `startUtc` values, but must still handle the conflict because of elapsed time and client/server clock differences.

The restore covers every part of the shift and only undoes a cancellation made while the schedule was running. A part cancelled because the schedule was ended belongs to that ending, so a shift containing one is refused entirely rather than partly restored. The cancellation and its reason stay in the schedule history. An optional note is recorded with the restore in schedule history and shown to the employees who are already notified about the restore. A company-scoped manager reads at the read tier: at least one assignee of the schedule must be within the manager's reach, or the schedule must have no assignees; otherwise the response is the not-found shape. stated scope, including an unscoped non-reshaping update; it is refused with HTTP 400 on
`confirmDiscard` in those cases.

assignmentsVisibleToTeamMembers.description:
Optional schedule-level employee-assignment visibility choice. Absence leaves the stored
value unchanged; an explicit JSON null is refused with HTTP 400 and the validation error is
addressed to `assignmentsVisibleToTeamMembers`.

jobCostTASegments.description:
Optional job-costing default, expressed as the ordered business values of the Time-Attendance
segments of the client's job-costing definition effective on the day the shift starts
(FR-49553-DRAFT-TECH-REV-03-1). Merge-patch presence has three decidable states: the property
absent from the JSON leaves the job-costing default unchanged; present as null or as an empty
array clears it; present as a non-empty array replaces the whole selection — there is no
element-wise merge.
The per-element rule is definition-dependent and is therefore enforced in the business layer
rather than by a single-field attribute: a count fault is reported on
`jobCostTASegments`, a value fault on `jobCostTASegments[index]`.

timeZoneId.description:
Optional preferred time-zone identifier. Independently optional: it may be supplied,
omitted, or explicitly cleared to null on its own (FR-49553-DRAFT-TECH-REV-01-2).

startUtc.description:
Optional canonical UTC start. In a FutureOccurrences patch, a present value configures the
fresh continuation and its UTC date must equal `effectiveFromUtc`; a mismatch returns
HTTP 400 with the validation error addressed to `startUtc`. When omitted, the server
rebases the existing proposed start—the current canonical start in that case—onto
`effectiveFromUtc` while preserving its UTC time of day.
 Data type is validated and must be Integer

endUtc.description:
Optional canonical UTC end. In a FutureOccurrences patch, a present value configures the
fresh continuation. When omitted, the server derives the continuation end from its resolved
start and the current source shift duration, preserving that duration.
 Data type is validated and must be Integer

repeatUntilDate.description:
Inclusive last recurrence date.
 Data type is validated and must be Number

Worklio.ApiModels.SCH.Models.Schedules.S.description:
JSON Merge Patch request for a Draft or published schedule. A published repeating schedule
requires a scope only when the patch sets a time, time-zone, recurrence, or rotation field.
Without such a field and without a scope, only the published schedule's non-reshaping content
is updated. For FutureOccurrences, the request describes the fresh linked continuation rather
than rewriting the original schedule in place; supplied time and recurrence values configure
that continuation.

rowVersion.description:
Required base64 concurrency token returned by the latest schedule read.
The decoded token must contain exactly 8 bytes.
